locations.name: Hawaiian Aroma Caffe at Waikiki Walls

risks.title: Market timing
risks.risk: F&B M&A multiples are sensitive to consumer-spending sentiment and interest-rate cycles. A 12-month delay could compress multiples 0.5–1.0x.
risks.mitigation: We track 30+ comparable processes and recommend launching when buyer-side capital is most active. Process can flex 6–8 weeks in either direction without losing tension.

risks.title: Key-person dependence
risks.risk: Buyers will price in founder-departure risk. Heavy reliance on the founder for sourcing, hiring, or customer relationships can discount EV by 10–15%.
risks.mitigation: QoE prep includes a documented bench inventory. We position rollover, advisory, or earn-out structures so the founder's continued role is a feature, not a contingency.

risks.title: Customer or channel concentration
risks.risk: Disproportionate revenue from a single channel, market, or wholesale account triggers diligence penalty and reps-and-warranties friction.
risks.mitigation: We surface concentration early, frame the diversification roadmap, and prepare the data room to defend each concentration as strategic rather than fragile.

risks.title: Working capital surprises
risks.risk: Buyers set a working-capital peg at LOI. Seasonal businesses with inventory or pre-paid lease cycles can give back $200–500K of headline EV at close.
risks.mitigation: We model the peg in advance against a trailing 12-month average and negotiate it as part of the LOI — not as a diligence afterthought.

risks.title: Diligence drag
risks.risk: Buyers extending exclusivity to re-trade is the most common late-stage failure mode. Each additional 30 days of diligence raises re-trade probability ~15%.
risks.mitigation: Sell-side QoE upfront, pre-built data room, and a competitive backup bidder in reserve. We do not concede exclusivity without a tight diligence timetable.

scripts.cover: Welcome. This deck was prepared by Focus West, a division of Focus Investment Banking, exclusively for Company A. Over the next ten minutes we'll show you what we believe your business is worth, how we'd run the process to get there, and what the outcome looks like for you personally. The goal of this conversation isn't to convince you to sell — it's to help you understand the choice you have, so when you're ready, you're ready.
scripts.snapshot: Before we say anything about ourselves, here's what we already know about you. Twelve locations across four Oregon markets. Average unit volume just over seven hundred eighty thousand. Founded in twenty fourteen, sixty-two team members, revenue compounding from four point eight million in twenty twenty-two to nine point three six million in twenty twenty-five. That's about a twenty-five percent compound annual growth rate. We say this because the rest of this conversation is grounded in the business you actually built, not a generic pitch.
scripts.team: The three of us are operators first, bankers second. Conor Miller scaled and exited Zamp Solar as chief operating officer. I built and exited Vidigo and Phantom Farms. Jared Peterson co-founded Cairn and spent a decade at Apple. We've been in your shoes — we know what it's like to take the call from your first inbound buyer, to wonder if you're being sold a multiple or a real number. The Focus Investment Banking platform behind us handles the institutional execution. We handle the conversation.
scripts.platform: Some context on the platform behind us. Focus Investment Banking has been around since nineteen eighty-two. Four hundred-plus deals closed across our partner team. Six billion in total transaction volume. Registered broker-dealer, FINRA-SIPC member. M and A Worldwide network reach across the US and Europe. The point of these numbers isn't to impress you — it's to say that when we put you in front of buyers, you're not a first-time deal for the firm.
scripts.values: Here's what we hear from every founder we work with. Six things matter, roughly in this order: protect the brand you built, reward the risk you took, find a buyer whose vision aligns with yours, minimize disruption to your team, preserve the culture that made this work, and certainty that the deal actually closes. You can drag these cards on screen to show us your real priority order. We'll design the process around what you actually care about, not what most lists say founders care about.
scripts.buyers: There are four buyer types we'll run in parallel. Strategics — coffee operators and adjacent food and beverage companies — they tend to move quickly when the fit is right. Private equity, both platform sponsors and add-on buyers, will underwrite the repeatability of your store model. Family offices bring patient capital and tolerance for operator-led structures. International acquirers from Europe and Asia pay premiums for brand stories that travel. We run all four in parallel — the single biggest determinant of price is having multiple credible bidders at the table.
scripts.process: Our process has three phases over roughly twenty-six weeks. Build the story — financial cleanup, quality-of-earnings prep, your unit economics narrative. Run the field — we contact forty to sixty buyers, hold eight to twelve management meetings, and guide first-round bids to a comparable structure so price emerges rather than being negotiated. Protect the outcome — best and final tightened against benchmarks, working capital peg negotiated up front, definitive documents to signed, funded, and done.
scripts.risks: Most bankers don't talk about what could go wrong. We do. Market timing — multiples are sensitive to consumer sentiment and rates. Key-person dependence — buyers price in founder-departure risk. Channel concentration — over-reliance on one market triggers diligence friction. Working capital surprises at the peg. And diligence drag — buyers extending exclusivity to re-trade is the most common late-stage failure. For each one, we have a documented mitigation. The point is we're not selling you certainty. We're selling you preparation.
scripts.drivers: Buyers underwrite eight value drivers, in roughly this order: same-store sales trend, store-level four-wall EBITDA, your unit economics — AUV, ticket, throughput, payback. Then brand and density, real estate and lease optionality, your forward pipeline, your team and systems, and finally channel mix. We translate each of these into the buyer's underwriting case, not just into a memo. Hover any card on screen to see the supporting trend.
scripts.valuation: Here's our preliminary view of value. Four point three to six point two million, blended EBITDA and revenue approach against your twenty twenty-five results. The EBITDA approach supports four point six to six point one. The revenue cross-check supports five point six to seven point five. There's a normalization opportunity if the twenty twenty-five cost pressure on outsourced labor and rent is reversible — that pushes you toward the higher end. You can drag the EBITDA multiple slider to see sensitivity in real time.
scripts.comps: Seven comparable transactions in the last four years. PJW Restaurant Group at six point four times EBITDA. Stumptown Coffee at five point eight times. Bluestone Lane at seven point two times — cross-border premium. Joe Coffee, Verve, Birch, La Colombe at eight point four — that one's the outlier because of CPG channel diversification. The bar chart shows where your valuation range sits relative to these. We're not cherry-picking favorable comps — we're showing you the full distribution.
scripts.scenarios: Three deal structures to consider. Full strategic sale — highest expected EV, cleanest break, six-month transition. PE recap with thirty percent rollover — cash now plus a second bite of the apple in four to seven years. Family office partial — operator-led, patient capital, lower headline but more founder alignment. Click each card to see the implications and how that structure flows through to your net proceeds.
scripts.waterfall: This is the slide that matters most. Headline EV is one number — your net proceeds is another. Starting from six point two million, subtract the working capital peg, existing debt, our success fee, closing costs. That gets you to equity proceeds. Multiply by your ownership stake. Subtract federal capital gains, subtract state tax. The number at the bottom — that's what hits your bank account. Drag transaction value, your ownership percent, basis, or state to see your real outcome.
scripts.terms: Most of our economics tie to closing. Eight thousand monthly retainer keeps the process resourced. Three point five percent minimum success fee tied to transaction value. Out-of-pocket expenses with budget approved up front. Mutual termination rights and a defined tail covering buyers we introduced. The fee calculator on screen shows what we make at different transaction values. The point — we win when you win, and we want you to see exactly how that math works.
scripts.roadmap: An indicative twenty-six-week roadmap. Weeks one through six — readiness. Financials cleaned, QoE prepped, story and buyer list drafted. Weeks seven through sixteen — go to market. Outreach, NDAs, CIM out, management meetings, first-round indications. Weeks seventeen through twenty-six — close. Best and final, exclusivity, diligence, working capital peg, definitive documents, signed and funded. The today indicator on the chart is draggable — slide it to project where we'd be if we started this week.
